LESSON: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFT

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.11: Indigenous Kenyan Craft

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Indigenous Kenyan Craft. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does basket making contribute to the economic well- being of communities?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify basketry items made using coil techniques
2. appreciate basketry as an indigenous craft in Kenya

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFT
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Indigenous Kenyan Craft helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFT
Study Indigenous Kenyan Craft like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify basketry items made using coil techniques

What this means
In this part you learn to identify basketry items made using coil techniques. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify basketry items made using coil techniques.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Indigenous Kenyan Craft” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify basketry items made using coil techniques. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate basketry as an indigenous craft in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate basketry as an indigenous craft in Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate basketry as an indigenous craft in Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Indigenous Kenyan Craft in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate basketry as an indigenous craft in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Indigenous Kenyan Craft is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Indigenous Kenyan Craft” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify basketry items made using coil techniques)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Indigenous Kenyan Craft in your own words. (skill: appreciate basketry as an indigenous craft in Kenya)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Indigenous Kenyan Craft to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify basketry items made using coil techniques.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate basketry as an indigenous craft in Kenya.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Indigenous Kenyan Craft from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Indigenous Kenyan Craft: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Indigenous Kenyan Craft?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does basket making contribute to the economic well- being of communities?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Indigenous Kenyan Craft means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify basketry items made using coil techniques.
5. Be able to: appreciate basketry as an indigenous craft in Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
